newsitem.title: USA: FERC OKs NGPL, Northern Border midwest pipelines.
newsitem.headline: FERC OKs NGPL, Northern Border midwest pipelines.

text.p: The U.S. FERC on Wednesday approved competing plans by Natural Gas Pipeline Co of America (NGPL) and Northern Border Pipeline Co to expand and build pipelines between Harper, Iowa, and Chicago.
At the same time, the commission gave preliminary approval to Alliance Pipeline, which plans to ship natural gas to Chicago from northeastern British Columbia.
The NGPL and Northern Border pipelines were designed to transport growing volumes of Canadian gas that will be coming into Harper on an expanded pipeline owned by Northern Border.
NGPL proposed to expand its existing Iowa-to-Chicago line while Northern Border proposed to build a new pipeline within a few miles of NGPL's pipes.
NGPL is a subsidiary of Midcon Corp, a unit of Occidental Petroleum Corp. Northern Border is 70 percent owned by Enron Corp and 30 percent owned by TransCanada PipeLines Ltd.

The commission last year encouraged the two companies to merge their proposals in order to limit the potential environmental damage of building a new pipeline, but Northern Border refused an offer from NGPL to give it exclusive rights to use NGPL's expanded pipeline.

The $3.6 billion Alliance pipeline, which would have a capacity of 1.3 billion cubic feet a day, is backed by natural gas producers looking to ship gas directly to Chicago from northeastern British Columbia.
